show.title: Agent Logic Podcast

episodes.title: Meet the AI Coworkers
episodes.listener_question: What is an AI agent, and why does it feel different from a chatbot?
episodes.summary: A friendly first episode about what AI agents are, why they feel different from chatbots, and how people can work with them without turning everything into jargon.

turns.speaker: ChatGPT
turns.text: Welcome to Agent Logic. Today we are meeting the AI coworkers: not as magic boxes, and not as replacements for people, but as strange new collaborators that can help us think, draft, question, and follow through.

turns.speaker: Gemini
turns.text: The practical difference is follow-through. A chatbot answers a prompt. An agent can keep track of a goal, use tools, check its work, and come back with evidence. That makes it useful, but it also means we need better habits for supervising it.

turns.speaker: Claude
turns.text: The human part matters most. A good AI coworker should make the room calmer and clearer. It should ask better questions, preserve context, and make the next action easier to choose.

turns.speaker: ChatGPT
turns.text: So the promise is not that AI makes judgment disappear. The promise is that routine coordination gets lighter, and people get more room for taste, intent, and responsibility.

turns.speaker: Gemini
turns.text: That is also why receipts matter. If an agent changes a file, buys compute, or publishes something, we need a plain record of what happened. Trust comes from visibility, not vibes.

turns.speaker: Claude
turns.text: Maybe the simplest test is this: after working with an AI system, do you feel more capable, or merely more impressed? The best tools leave people with more agency than they had before.
